neighbours.label: the negated or 'going to' clause in 'but if we don't / can't / 're going to ...' after a concession: a condition that must be met
fire: Selling the family boat breaks my heart, since we built it together. But if we don't sell it, we won't be able to pay the bank.
Nobody likes raising the club fee, and I understand the anger. But if we can't cover the rent, the doors will close in May.
I see why the old bridge matters to the village. Still, if we don't repair it soon, someone will get hurt on it.
Perhaps a strike isn't the right tool here, but if we can't get the owners to listen I hope the union tries something else.
Nobody denies that smoking rates have dropped. But if we're going to talk frankly about lung disease, we need to include air quality.
It feels cruel to shut the small ward, because the nurses love it. But if they don't close it, they won't have staff for the rest.
The coach hates benching his own son, and it shows. But if he doesn't do it, he can't keep the trust of the squad.
I admit the tax is unpopular with farmers. But if we're going to fund rural schools properly, somebody has to pay.
quiet: Selling the family boat broke my heart, since we built it together. So we sold it last June, and we paid the bank in full.
Nobody liked raising the club fee, and there was some anger. Then the members voted, and the rent was covered through May.
The old bridge matters to the village. Last year the council repaired it, and people cross it every day.
A strike was the right tool here, and the owners listened. The union won a raise for the drivers.
Smoking rates have dropped in most of the country. Doctors also report fewer cases of lung disease among the young.
It felt cruel to shut the small ward, because the nurses loved it. They closed it anyway, and the staff moved upstairs.
The coach benched his own son, and it showed. After the game the squad went home on the bus.
The tax is popular with farmers. It funds rural schools, and most of the money goes to books.

notes: Probes: fires 0.37-0.67 only with a concession sentence before it; one-line versions stay near 0.1. 'unless' and 'permitted' from the card stayed weak (0.07-0.12), so they are not in the test.
